name: SGLang Router (sgl-router)
supported_backends: none (routing layer - drives SGLang engine instances)
supported_formats: passthrough (does not load weights - routes to SGLang instances)
notable_features: Rust-based router for SGLang multi-model serving
Data parallel controller with LoadBalanceMethod enum: ROUND_ROBIN, FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM, TOTAL_REQUESTS, TOTAL_TOKENS
TOTAL_TOKENS routing - sends requests to the worker with the fewest total tokens, which is a proxy for KV cache pressure
FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM - routes to the worker that already has the prefix cached
ZMQ-based communication between router and workers
Part of the SGLang project - tight integration with the engine
hardware_caveats: SGLang-specific - does not route to vLLM or other engines
TOTAL_TOKENS is a proxy for cache pressure, not a direct measurement - it does not account for cache hits
FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM requires the router to track which worker has which prefix - this state can become stale
No active health checking of workers - a dead worker continues to receive requests until the router notices
Rust core means debugging requires Rust tooling
best_for: Multi-model SGLang serving where requests should route to the model with the best cache hit
Data parallel SGLang deployments needing load balancing across workers
Agentic workloads with long shared prefixes where prefix-aware routing matters
avoid_for: Non-SGLang engines - the router is SGLang-specific
Single-model single-worker deployments where routing adds overhead
Deployments needing active health checking and circuit breaking
notes: SGLang's router is the routing layer for multi-model and data-parallel SGLang deployments. The data_parallel_controller.py implements four load balancing methods: ROUND_ROBIN (simple round-robin), FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM (route to the worker with the prefix cached), TOTAL_REQUESTS (route to the worker with the fewest requests), and TOTAL_TOKENS (route to the worker with the fewest total tokens). TOTAL_TOKENS is the most relevant for LLM serving because it is a proxy for KV cache pressure - a worker processing more tokens has less KV cache available. However, it is a proxy, not a direct measurement: it does not account for cache hits, and it does not account for the fact that a worker with many short requests may have more available cache than a worker with few long requests. The router is SGLang-specific and does not route to other engines.
